generalDropOff.residentRequirement: Baltimore City residents with valid IDs only.
generalDropOff.feeNote: Effective November 1, 2025, a fee of $135 per ton applies to commercial haulers and residents disposing of non-hazardous solid waste at Quarantine Road Landfill. City residents may continue to dispose of recycling, electronics, appliances, and household waste at DPW's five Residential Drop-off Centers at no cost.
acceptedAtResidentialCenters: Yard waste that is bagged appropriately
Oyster shells (Sisson Street Drop-Off Center only)
notAcceptedAtRegularResidentialDropOff: Any other solid, liquid, or gaseous substance regulated as hazardous by State or federal law
generalDropOff.hhwNote: Some items may be recycled during household hazardous waste collection days (see hhw).

scheduleRule.when: First Friday and Saturday of each month
scheduleRule.holidayNote: Dates may be adjusted for holidays.

hhw.businesses: Businesses and commercial users must use a private vendor.
hhw.packagingRule: All materials must be in original packaging with manufacturer's label. No unmarked or leaking containers will be accepted.
acceptable: Automotive fluids (antifreeze, transmission and power brake fluid, used motor oil)
hhw.fluorescentBulbNote: City strongly urges residents to recycle fluorescent light bulbs at Northwest Residential Recycling Center on household hazardous waste collection days.

hardToRecycle.title: Hard Plastic
hardToRecycle.guidance: Hard plastic items like buckets, laundry baskets, and water bottles cannot be left at the curb. Take them to a Citizen Drop-Off Center in the container labeled Rigid Plastics.

hardToRecycle.title: Scrap Metal and White Goods
hardToRecycle.guidance: Large appliances (white goods) and scrap metal should be taken to drop-off centers for recycling.

hardToRecycle.title: Household Hazardous Waste
hardToRecycle.guidance: Items like bleach, paint, and batteries must not go in the trash; follow hazardous waste safety and recycling rules.

hardToRecycle.title: Food Scraps
hardToRecycle.guidance: Consider composting or food scrap recycling instead of landfill disposal.

hardToRecycle.title: Tires
hardToRecycle.guidance: All tires must be off rim. Up to four off-rim tires per month at an accepting recycling center, or set out four for bulk trash collection (call 311).

hardToRecycle.title: Textiles
hardToRecycle.guidance: Used clothes, shoes, towels, and sheets at any of DPW's five Residential Drop-Off Centers.

hardToRecycle.title: Motor Oil
hardToRecycle.guidance: Up to five quarts of used motor oil at any of Baltimore's five Residential Recycling Centers.

hardToRecycle.title: Mattresses and Box Springs
hardToRecycle.guidance: Drop off clean and dry mattresses and box springs for recycling.

hardToRecycle.title: Electronics
hardToRecycle.guidance: eCycling for computers, TVs, and similar electronics at drop-off centers.

dataLimitations.perSiteDailyMaterialCalendar: City pages do not publish a per-site daily calendar of which materials are accepted on which weekdays. Warnings use published open days/hours plus HHW and hard-to-recycle rules.
